newsitem.title: USA: Rite Aid sees no acquisitions next year.
newsitem.headline: Rite Aid sees no acquisitions next year.

text.p: Rite Aid Inc, which earlier announced an agreement to buy Thrifty PayLess Inc for $1.4 billion, said on Monday it did not plan to make any acquisitions next year.

"We're going to be occupied all next year with Thrifty PayLess, so I don't anticipate looking at any acquisitions of any size at all next year," Chief Executive Officer Martin Grass told more than 250 investors and analysts in a telephone conference call.

Grass also backed Wall Street estimates that Rite Aid will earn $2.43 per share in its fiscal year ending February 1998. He said the company set a target of $2.95 EPS for the year ending February 1999.
Grass also said Rite Aid would adhere to Thrifty PayLess' plans to open 30 new stores next year, but would then accelerate the expansion program.

"We expect to grow the combined business at a faster rate than Rite Aid was going to grow on its own," he said, adding that the eventual plan will call for Rite Aid to open 100 new stores on the East Coast and 100 new stores on the West Coast annually.
Rite Aid also is replacing some of its East Coast stores with larger facilities.
